entries.title: Fixed dollar-figure text corrupting meta tags on matter/record pages
entries.why: audit.json's weakDescription list (10 pages) included 7 matter pages with implausibly short char counts (live-137: 2, live-203: 11). `grep -rl 'content="[^"]*<meta ' matters/ chapter-11/ federal-cases/` found 31 published pages where a second <meta name="description" content="..."> fragment was spliced into the first one's attribute value. Root cause: build_matter_pages.ts/build_record_pages.ts build title/description/OG/Twitter/canonical tags with .replace(regex, templateString) using a literal "$1" to reinsert the matched opening tag; "$1" is special to String.replace, so a summary containing a dollar figure like "$170M" has its digit read as a second backreference. This was backlog item 5's real cause, not thin content.
entries.metric: audit.summary.weakDescription

verdict.note: Confirmed same-day: the prerender workflow rebuilt all matter/record pages from the fixed builder (commit 0c21e23) within minutes of the push. Live site_audit.py: weakDescription 10 -> 3, and the 3 remaining are exactly the pages flagged as a separate, still-open issue (contact.html, handbook-success.html, reset-password.html), not this fix's targets. entries.title: Analyzed why v4.3 misses the final-outcome range 47% of the time; wrote evidence and proposed prompt changes to ops/calculator-proposals.md (NEEDS JEFF)
entries.why: ops/metrics/goals.json (2026-10-15): calculator is the goal furthest behind (gap 0.646, finalRangeHitRate 0.531/target 0.75, calculatorViews7 0/target 50) and untouched by the last 2 log entries (imp-009 traffic, imp-010 conversion); audit was clean. Backlog G3. The valuation method can't be changed from this session (CLAUDE.md) and no change can be deployed from the cloud, so per the playbook's calculator scope this replayed the already-scored, already-published v4.3 backtest results (js/backtest-results-data.js, no new API calls or spend) to find the actual miss pattern rather than guessing. Found two dominant, case-cited patterns across the 15/32 misses: (1) a one-sided party figure (loan principal, punitive prayer, a second rent claim) priced at high confidence as if it directly equalled the award, with no issue modeling the legal theory that actually capped recovery (donegal-v-christie-scott 80x over, can-iv-packard-square 1.6x over, wheeler-reit 2x+ over, 1700-market-v-common-grounds 14x over); (2) in dueling-valuation disputes, when only one side's appraisal figure gets quoted into the record the existing competing-figures basis never triggers and the range anchors to one side only (kks-properties, elpa-builders miss this way; hrt-enterprises, state-v-skyway capture both sides and hit). Two smaller findings (immaterial-issue floor creep on near-exact hits; undercounted multi-claim cases) are documented too. This is evidence plus a proposal, not a code change -- nothing in the calculator's prompt or math was touched.
entries.metric: none directly -- this did not change the live site or the valuation method; what to check next time is whether Jeff has reviewed ops/calculator-proposals.md and ruled on the proposed prompt changes

entries.title: Fixed a scoring bug in replay_backtest.py, then matched-case-set comparison of v4.3 vs v6
entries.why: goals.json mostBehind today: conversion, calculator, traffic, news. Judged imp-013 (no clear effect) and imp-014 (helped) first, both checkAfter today. After those closures every single goal still had an open watching entry (traffic: imp-009; conversion: imp-020/imp-022; calculator: imp-011/imp-016/imp-025/imp-026; subscription: imp-015; news: imp-017), so per the one-open-experiment-per-goal backlog rule this run worked evidence/backlog work instead of shipping a new tracked page/code change -- and 2026-10-22's own entry (imp-026) had explicitly flagged its v4.3-vs-v6 comparison as confounded by unequal case sets (v6's full 98-case results-v6/ vs v4.3's older, smaller 47-case results-v4.3/ snapshot) and worth resolving for free. While building a matched comparison (all 47 v4.3 case IDs are a subset of v6's 98), found scripts/replay_backtest.py's rep_priced/opp_priced/unpriced_claim checks called issue_range() without the as_of argument the main loop uses two lines above -- for v6-style role-tagged figures (credit/cap, no plain amount) this silently fell back to v4-only logic and disagreed with the main loop, scoring can-iv-packard-square-v-schubiner-2021 as a numeric miss when the live v6 model itself had already correctly returned no estimate (damagesRange: null) for that case. Fixed by passing the same as_of value to all three checks (3 lines). Verified no regression before trusting it: zero results-v4.3 files have role-tagged figures (grep confirmed), and results-v4.3 alone still replays to exactly 19/32 final hits, the already-published figure. Then re-ran the matched comparison on the identical 44 cases: overall final-hit rate is close (61.3% v4.3 vs 64.5% v6, far below the unmatched 72.2% headline), but training cases improve a lot (62.5% -> 79.2%) while the 7 matched held-out cases get worse (57.1% -> 14.3%) -- a possible overfitting signal on a small sample, not proof. No API spend -- all free replay of already-saved backtest result files. Full numbers, per-case detail and two new NEEDS JEFF notes written to ops/calculator-proposals.md; backlog G15 updated with the corrected comparison.

Per the one-open-experiment-per-goal rule, worked backlog/evidence work not measured by a goal metric instead: picked up 2026-10-25's own flagged-but-unconfirmed windsor-tower-v-speedy-maintenance-2024 flip (G15) rather than another social-drafts refresh, since G3/G15 evidence work has concretely found and documented real bugs almost every time it's been tried.

entries.note: Hand-traced the saved results-v6/windsor-tower-v-speedy-maintenance-2024.json prediction against the live code (no API spend): Speedy's single $66,000 disputed mechanics-lien claim is pled as three alternative opposing legal theories (contract breach, unjust enrichment, lien foreclosure), each an independent issue with the same figure and probabilityRange. dedupeRepresentedFigures() (valuation-math.ts line 85) explicitly skips opposing issues, so index.ts's mechanical per-issue loop (lines ~2776-2793) sums each theory's expected-value contribution separately -- 3 x (0.2 * -66000) = -39600 instead of one -13200 -- and the arithmetic reproduces the saved damagesRange[0]=-18138 to the dollar. Confirmed this is in the shared aggregation step (not v6IssueRange), so v4.3/v4.4 share the same latent bug; it just hasn't shown up in any scored v4.3 case yet. No code changed (Jeff-gated, and not cloud-deployable regardless). Full trace and proposed fix shape (merge same-figure alternative opposing theories into one issue before the mechanical loop, same pattern dedupeRepresentedFigures already uses for the represented side) in ops/calculator-proposals.md's 2026-10-26 entry; G15 updated with a fourth concrete decision.
